Logan / Ben — reviewed AcroHealth's redlines and attached a proposed legal response (Proposed_Redlines_kpark_20280504.docx). High-level:

1) Invoice entity: We can accommodate invoicing to a customer-designated entity, but we need: (a) a representation in the Order Form that the invoicing entity is the party responsible for payment (Customer Entity), and (b) a PO or remittance instructions from AcroHealth B.V. confirming that billing path. That protects us from downstream collection risk.

Suggested language: "Invoices may be rendered to the Customer entity specified in the Order Form. The entity so-specified represents and warrants that it is responsible for payment of Fees. Redwood shall not be liable for delayed payment resulting from the Customer's internal entity routing."

2) VAT / withholding: We cannot broadly accept a clause that allows unilateral withholding without evidence. Recommended approach: allow withholding to the extent required by applicable law, and require the Customer to provide withholding certificates or evidence. Also add a gross-up or invoice adjustment process if withholding results in net payment shortfall. Sample: "If Customer is required by law to withhold taxes from payments, Customer shall (a) notify Redwood promptly, (b) withhold only to the extent required by law, and (c) provide Redwood with official documentation evidencing the withholding. To the extent withholding reduces the net amount Redwood receives, the parties will work in good faith to adjust the invoiced amount so Redwood receives the full Fees (net of the required withholdings)."

3) Net terms exception: Net 45 increases credit exposure. Finance must sign off. If Sales is willing to accept Net 45 we should get one of: (i) a PO with an AP contact and remittance schedule, (ii) increased commitment (e.g., +15% ARR), or (iii) short-term credit facility or partial upfront.

I've flagged this for Finance review and attached our proposed redlines. If AcroHealth insists on Net 45 with no other concession, I recommend escalating to Sales Leadership for approval.

—Kim
Kimberly Park

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and Kim's proposed language. AcroHealth can provide a PO and remittance instructions from AcroHealth B.V. We cannot accept a gross-up requirement as a condition for withholding (local tax authority requires withholding in certain cases). Our position is: if withholding is required by law, we will withhold and provide official documentation; we can't agree to increase the invoice to cover local tax.

Net 45 is a firm requirement from Procurement. We are prepared to sign now (attached: AH_Signed_OrderForm_2028-05-09.pdf) if Redwood can:
- Invoice AcroHealth B.V. as the billing entity;
- Allow withholding where required by law and accept the withholding documentation as sufficient;
- Accept Net 45 for this Order Form.

If Redwood needs a PO + prepay as a tradeoff, please confirm immediately — we can request an exception from our AP team but prefer to avoid delays.

Best,
Carla

We cannot accept a blanket refusal to allow an adjustment where withholding leaves Redwood short; however, for pragmatic deal-flow we will accept the withholding documentation as sufficient and treat this as a one-off settlement process for this Order Form.
- Net terms: Finance requires an exception to our standard Net 30. I've looped in finance@redwood.ai for approval of Net 45 for this deal. Finance, please review the attached signed OF and confirm whether Net 45 is approved as-is or if we need PO + first-invoice prepay.

Next steps: Finance will respond within 48 hours. If approved, we will issue invoices to AcroHealth B.V. under Net 45 and proceed with onboarding. If Finance requires PO+prepay, we'll notify you immediately so AcroHealth can provide a PO or alternate arrangement.
